The All Farmers Association of Nigeria has praised the Federal Government for coming to the aid of 4,000 members whose farms were recently destroyed by flooding. The AFAN Chairman in Ekiti State, Mr Sunday Adekogbon, thanked the FG, the National Agricultural Development Fund and the state government for supporting the affected farmers with farm inputs to enable them to pick up after the disaster. The FG had, through the agency, at an event tagged ‘NADF intervention for flood-affected farmers in Ekiti State’ on Saturday, distributed emergency farm inputs to 4,000 smallholder farmers affected by flooding in the state to help restore their farms and improve food production. Items distributed to the affected farmers include 4,000 bags of NPK fertiliser, 4,000 bags of urea, 2,800 bags of rice seeds, 1,200 bags of maize seeds, 4,000 bottles of pre-plant chemicals, 4,000 bottles of pre-emergence herbicides, 4,000 bottles of early post-emergence herbicides and 4,000 bottles of insecticide. The AFAN chairman urged beneficiaries not to sell the inputs, but to use them for their intended agricultural purposes. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources Adekogbon, while appreciating NADF for the gesture, said, “The support will enable farmers to contribute more effectively to food security.” The affected farmers, represented by Mr Ojo Falana, expressed appreciation for the intervention. Falana said, “We appreciate the NADF for this gesture, and we promise to use the agricultural inputs judiciously to improve our farming activities and achieve the programme’s objectives.” FG to service $500m World Bank loan until 2050 Don urges AI solutions for rural healthcare Ekiti youths get grants to drive economy Speaking earlier, NADF Executive Secretary and Chief Executive Officer, Mr Muhammed Ibrahim, represented by the Head of Strategy, Planning, Evaluation, Monitoring and Learning, Mrs Adebanke Fajana, urged the beneficiaries to “use the materials for the purpose meant to justify government’s investment,” saying the gesture was to ensure recovery. Speaking on the essence of the intervention, Ibrahim said, “For many farmers, this loss is threatening not only the current production cycle, but also the ability to prepare for the next production cycle. “Without timely intervention, this disaster can easily become a crisis that lasts for seasons. We are here to ensure that recovery is done.” Ibrahim added, “We want you to see renewed opportunity. We encourage you to see farms being restored to productivity. We encourage you to see families regaining their livelihood, and we see communities strengthened against failure shocks. Above all, we see a pathway towards more resilient and food-secure Nigeria. ” The NADF boss said the intervention aligned with President Bola Tinubu’s vision “to protect livelihoods, strengthen food security and build a resilient agricultural economy under the Renewed Hope Agenda.” The Special Adviser to Ekiti State Governor Biodun Oyebanji on Agriculture, Boluwade Ebenezer, said the intervention would restore the affected farmers’ confidence, boost agricultural production and strengthen food security in Ekiti State and Nigeria.
